transcript_body:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Aperture Head of ML), Daniel Kim (Platform Eng), Priya Rao (CTO)

[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Morgan, i'll run the commercial side and Ravi's our SE.
[00:12] Ravi: hi all, yeah, i'll focus on the measurement plan and infra. apologies if i'm a bit terse, got a weird connection.
[00:20] Sofia: no problem, thanks. we wanna lock down acceptance criteria for the POC — mainly latency for chat queries and per-token cost tradeoffs.
[00:28] Daniel: and we need to understand how replay vs synthetic will affect tails, like the p99.
[00:36] Morgan: cool. high-level proposal — two-week run: 3 days synthetic load shaping to validate topology, then 7-day replay of production traces, with TTFT and TPOT measured independently. thoughts?
[00:50] Priya: sounds reasonable, but timeline depends on our ability to sanitize traces; can we do a shorter synthetic-only first?
[00:58] Ravi: yep, that aligns. synthetic gives quick iteration. re replay, we recommend sampling windows to keep cost down — not full 30 days at once.
[01:10] Sofia: we have about 48 hours of representative logs from last quarter; we can anonymize those.
[01:18] Morgan: excellent. on SLOs, are you leaning to a TTFT-first acceptance or per-token? we usually ask customers to pick primary gate — which one blocks rollout?
[01:30] Sofia: primary is user perceived latency — TTFT — but product also cares about per-token cost for scale. so both matter.
[01:38] Daniel: agree. p95 user latency target of around 250ms would be great; p99 under 600ms. is that feasible?
[01:48] Ravi: depends on model and seq length. with quantized 8-bit medium models on dedicated A100s we typically see p95 under 220ms for 64-token prompts in our internal traces, p99 around 450-500ms under steady-state. but your profile might skew longer — e.g., many long context interactions.
[02:05] Morgan: note that TTFT here means time-to-first-token measured at the API gateway to first token delivered to client. TPOT mean per-token latency aggregated across output tokens and impacts throughput. we define TPOT p95 as per-token on generation path.
[02:22] Sofia: can you give an example acceptance matrix? like what passes, what marginal, what fails?
[02:30] Ravi: sure: PASS if TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 600ms AND TPOT p95 <= 12ms per token and average CPU/GPU utilization under 70% at target concurrency. MARGINAL if TTFT p95 between 250-350ms or p99 600-800ms, or TPOT p95 12-18ms. FAIL if TTFT p95 > 350ms or p99 > 800ms persistently.
[02:58] Priya: those numbers look okay but can we tie cost per 1M tokens thresholds too? we need economic guardrails.
[03:06] Morgan: yes, we will include cost/unit estimates for the benchmark run and a projected per-1M token cost at target config.
[03:14] Daniel: will caching affect the SLOs? our app sees repeated prefixes a lot.
[03:20] Ravi: good catch — we will run two modes: cold (no prefix cache) and warm (KV/prefix cache enabled) and report both TTFT/TPOT. POC acceptance should focus on cold path for conservative gating but we note warm path improvements.
[03:36] Sofia: how about sample sizes — how many requests to measure p99 robustly?
[03:42] Ravi: for p99 you'd want at least 100k relevant samples during the replay window; if your trace set is smaller we'll augment with stratified synthetic requests to hit the tail.
[03:54] Morgan: logistics: Redwood provisions a dedicated test cluster in us-east for the test. aperture provides sanitized traces. we'll run an initial low-concurrency smoke then ramp.
[04:06] (crosstalk)
[04:10] Speaker 1: uh so the measurement scripts, are they open? can we run them in our infra?
[04:16] Ravi: yes, we share the harness (python + k6 snippets) and instructions; you can run locally or through our provisioned infra. results are CSV + Kibana dashboard export.
[04:28] Priya: need to confirm SOC2 implications — will logs/transcripts be stored?
[04:34] Morgan: for POC we keep logs for 30 days encrypted at rest; we can limit retention or provide on-prem artifacts on request. we'll also provide a security pack with SOC2 details.
[04:44] Sofia: ok good. any concerns about tokenization differences affecting TPOT? we saw weird token counts across models.
[04:50] Ravi: yes tokenization matters; we'll normalize by using the exact tokenizer used in the model variant and report tokens per prompt. we also capture model variant mapping (e.g., quantized vs fp16).
[04:59] Daniel: what about traffic shaping — do we replicate bursts?
[05:04] Ravi: the plan: use a load profile with three buckets — baseline steady qps, short bursts (5x for 30s), and cold-start injections. we'll define the burst cadence to mirror your observed peaks.
[05:16] Sofia: do you measure tail latency isolation — i.e., p99 excluding queuing vs including queuing?
[05:22] Ravi: we report both: server-side generation latency (excludes queue wait) and end-to-end API latency (includes queue/wait). p99 gating should be on end-to-end but we expose server-only to debug.
[05:34] Morgan: let's talk risks briefly. we see three primary risks: R1 trace fidelity (sanitized traces may remove pathological cases), R2 VPC peering window (timing may push replay later), R3 measurement noise from cloud noisy neighbors. mitigation: for R1 we augment with stratified synthetic tails; R2 we align on maintenance window; R3 we run multiple repeats and use median of medians.
[05:58] Priya: good. also note procurement — we may need a simple MSA addendum before we run a multi-day dedicated cluster.
[06:06] Morgan: understood, we'll send a light SOW and an MSA checklist.
[06:12] (brief pause)
[06:18] Sofia: can you also share an example benchmark report so our PMs know the format?
[06:23] Morgan: yes, we'll attach a template.
[06:26] Daniel: timeline recapped?
[06:29] Ravi: customer provides traces by 2026-10-10; Redwood provisions cluster and sends harness by 2026-10-12; synthetic smoke on 2026-10-13, then 7-day replay starting 2026-10-19 pending VPC.
[06:43] Sofia: sounds good. one more question — do you run model variant fallbacks automatically if a node degrades?
[06:50] Ravi: Redwood has routing policies; for POC we'll run with strict config (no automatic fallback) to measure baseline, then run a second pass with fallback to observe graceful degradation.
[07:02] Morgan: final quick recap — acceptance gates: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms; TPOT p95 <= 12ms per token. cold-path is primary. deliverables: harness, dashboards, SOW, security pack. action items and dates in the notes. thanks everyone.
[07:20] Priya: thanks.
[07:22] Sofia: thanks, bye.

End transcript. Some minor transcription artifacts present (Speaker 1 label where not resolved).
